knowledge_gaps: With nested negative sets, target rank cannot improve and HR@10 cannot increase as depth grows. The audit needs a sampling-based reference or normalized statistic to distinguish this expected effect from meaningful ranking weakness. Potential 8/10 is optimistic without evidence connecting these in-sample diagnostics to held-out improvements.

Reproduction requires explicit user/prefix sampling limits, history truncation, candidate distribution, frequency-bin boundaries, tie handling, bootstrap settings and runtime limits. A single candidate draw leaves sampling uncertainty unmeasured; restoring global RNG states may also leave loader-owned generators advanced. Difficulty 3/10 may underestimate these controls.

Excluding every training interaction from historical-prefix negative pools uses interactions occurring after the prefix. This is permissible training data, but changes the diagnostic population and can make ranking easier. Training memorization and popularity shortcuts remain alternative explanations; the proposed audit cannot establish current intent or compatibility.
